audit.coding_note: Runtime includes externally tracked object position; no held-out contact topology or independently measured load allocation. Same-recipe PPO is not a matched history/representation baseline.

inclusions.synthesis: A shared RMA latent provides a useful bimanual baseline without explicit tactile graphs. The teacher receives object identity/properties, orientation and contact impulses; the student uses 50-step observation/action history and wrist depth. Crucially, runtime object position still comes from an external camera/AprilTag (III-A/B; VI). Table I reports four-seed simulation success: Pick 65.74%, Lift 85.13%, Stack 3.81%; the unconditioned PPO baseline receives the same randomization/training recipe but lacks latent conditioning. Success means achieving the condition at least once during an episode. Hardware evidence is 14/20 lifts of one box, with stability required; failures include two slips and four oscillatory completions (VI). The study varies properties within a predefined object set, not held-out topology or broad unseen categories (VII). Reviewer inference: include as deployment-observable latent-system-identification baseline, while separating tracker-assisted control, training contact rewards, and force-aware tactile representations. No independent load-sharing estimate, causal force attribution, or hardware baseline is established.
inclusions.artifact_note: No code/data execution or independent workshop programme verification performed.

bib.author: Chen, Bo and Hu, Huanzhang and Ma, Junyang and Yue, Bo and Yu, Fangdi and Chen, Haijier and Lai, Xianxin and Pan, Shuyu and Yang, Zhen and Sun, Xiaoquan and Cui, Wenze and Jiang, Zhongliang and Liu, Shaopeng and Chen, Jiayu

audit.coding_note: Relative intensity and instability proxy are not calibrated force/slip. Human-tactile ablation does not isolate online robot tactile feedback. Table IV has 88.1% versus prose 88.3% discrepancy; no held-out sensor/topology test established.

inclusions.synthesis: TACROSS aligns heterogeneous human/robot sensing through anatomy-based contact fields, validity masks, sensor adapters, and a causal temporal/inter-finger Transformer (III-C). Its intensity and instability channels are relative/proxy quantities, not calibrated force or measured slip. ACT deploys robot RGB, proprioception and tactile history; robot demonstrations provide action ground truth, while retargeted human targets are auxiliary pseudo-labels (III-D). Four single-hand real tasks test dispensing, liquid transfer, pipetting and fruit handling (IV-A). At fixed 30 robot/150 human demonstrations, Table IV reports 91.9% mean success versus 73.1% without human tactile input and 49.4% without semantic alignment. The 16/160 condition's listed tasks average 88.125%, agreeing with table 88.1%, not prose 88.3%. Only the separate fruit-budget experiment explicitly states 40 rollouts/configuration; seed and broader split details are not established. Reviewer inference: add canonicalization/masking and human-data alignment baselines, but do not infer unseen-sensor, cross-hand/topology generalization, independent physical-label validation, or necessity of online robot touch from human-input ablations.
inclusions.artifact_note: Official project https://tacross-touch-project.github.io/ Resources states hardware, code and data planned, repository/download links to follow (checked Oct14). This conflicts with paper I statement that designs are available; do not mark artifacts released. Paper Table II reports 183.95 h total (159.09 h human + 24.86 h robot), separate from training subsets.

inclusions.synthesis: TouchScale reports 500h of synchronized human RGB-D/wrist video and bimanual normal-pressure data (3.1-3.2). Cross-sensor evaluation pools native grids into 12 fixed anatomical regions; pressure labels use sequence-maximum normalization (Appendix6). Size-matched approximately 16 h training gives EgoTactile contact IoU 0.181 versus 0.134, whereas the headline 0.383 uses full-scale training (4.1/Table 2/Fig4). Thus scale and dataset identity must be separated. Action-free future-touch mid-training followed by identical 50-demonstration/task robot post-training raises average success 22.5%→57.5%, with 20 trials/task on one xArm6/Revo2 platform (4.3/Table 4). Deployment uses current touch; future changes supervise training (Appendix10.2). Bimanual human collection does not establish bimanual robot control. Future-touch/action-error association is weak, and retrieval Top-10 differs from physical prediction accuracy (4.3; Appendix9). Reviewer inference: valuable data-scale and anatomical-evaluation baselines, but no independent wrench/load-transfer labels, matched-total-compute tactile causality, or held-out contact topology. The v2 date qualifies as revision discovery; no v1-v2 content change is claimed.
inclusions.artifact_note: Official project links verified: https://github.com/phai-lab/touchscale and https://huggingface.co/datasets/2077AIDataFoundation/TouchScale . audit.evidence_locator: III-A/B eqs1-5 and Automatic expert routing; III-C; IV-A; IV-B/Table I; IV-C/Table II; IV-D/Table III; V
audit.coding_note: Training labels expand force threshold events with future frames; pipette runtime router is causal. Wiping switch is manual. Contact rates and volume MAE have conditional denominators; grasp-height OOD is not topology OOD.

inclusions.synthesis: DEFT-VLA separates a frozen task-adapted base expert from a force-specialized contact expert, conditioning the latter on projected wrist-wrench history (III-A/B). Force-threshold labels include temporal look-ahead during training; learned pipette routing uses causal observations. Whiteboard wiping instead uses manually triggered expert switching (IV-A; V). The contact-localized blur/state-masking curriculum should be compared against simple force tokens and global curricula, with expert capacity and routing controlled. Using identical demonstrations and 20 trials/task, overall success is 70% tip attachment, 50% bimanual aspiration and 90% wiping (Table I). Contact-stage rates condition on reaching contact; aspiration 104 μL MAE covers successful trials only. Held-out grasp heights yield 5/10 successes on each pipette task, representing configuration change rather than topology OOD (IV-C). State-mask ablation improves tip-attachment success 15%→70% (IV-D), but no training-seed uncertainty is reported. Reviewer inference: this is real cooperative tool-actuation evidence and a stage-aware baseline, not validated cross-interface load inference, automatic routing on every task, or calibrated force safety.

audit.coding_note: Task-configured compliance, not learned cross-hand inference. Comp.Applied imitates corrected actions with stiff runtime controller. Turns/episode are not binary success. Table 2 trial allocation unspecified; card percentages incompatible with 50 trials per condition.

inclusions.synthesis: FOMO-Dex applies task-configured directional admittance to wrist/fingertip force feedback, preserving nominal motion in excluded directions (3.2-3.3). Single-hand experiments cover card pickup, cutting, nut rotation and screwdriving. The isotropic-compliance control shares sensing, rates and applicable admittance parameters, making direction selection a useful baseline (4.1). Results show force/progress tradeoffs: nut rotation is lower than stiff control, while screwdriving improves; minimum force exceedance is not universal best task performance (Table 2; 4.2). Force thresholds are operational limits, not validated safety guarantees. Four participants undergo randomized controller/task order before/after practice (4.3). With 50 demonstrations/setting, corrected-action imitation attains 67% card lift success over 18 trials, versus 0% for raw commands with online compliance; corrected-action policies use stiff deployment control (4.4). Rotation outcomes use 10 trials and measure turns, not completion. Reviewer inference: separate directional compliance, demonstration quality and action-target representation. Contact directions/targets remain configured, with no held-out topology or independent load-inference audit. Table 2’s50-trial wording does not resolve per-condition card denominators.

bibtex_fields.title: PACE: Temporal-Role Tactile Conditioning for Chunk-Based Insertion Policies

inclusions.synthesis: PACE separates a tactile stream into smoothed state conditioning, event-driven action residuals, and future-contact prediction during training. On five real insertion tasks, it reports 136/150 successes versus 69/150 for tactile concatenation, with common demonstrations and control frequency. Its strongest contribution is a controlled temporal-organization baseline, not spatial contact structure. Appendix A.6 reruns the complete ACT policy each control step, so the event pathway should not be described as a separately asynchronous reflex. Models are selected separately for task and geometry-clearance configurations; alternative force/current inputs do not establish zero-shot sensor transfer. Future-contact prediction is absent at inference. Wilson rollout intervals, force-stop-as-failure accounting, and demonstration-quality controls improve interpretability; independent training-seed variation, held-out topology, and calibrated contact safety remain untested.
details: Official abstract page gives v1 on Monday, 12 October 2026 at 07:35:21 UTC, with no later version. Four authors agree between abstract and full text. The Comments field claims CoRL 2026 acceptance; no independent venue confirmation was performed.

Inputs and labels: global/wrist RGB, 7D proprioception and default 6D GF225 contact-force vector. EMA alpha .05, history four samples; event gate uses normalized difference + norm and residual uses flattened history; correction prefix five of twenty actions. Future tactile increments supervise decoder only; head removed at inference (§§3.1-3.5).

Evaluation: Realman RM75 + Robotiq Hand-E, five tasks ~160 demos each, 30 rollouts each; socket randomized within demonstrated 25x25mm workspace. Six ManipulationNet geometry-clearance settings each 25 rollouts. C.2 selects individual checkpoint per 11 task/configurations; no held-out task/geometry transfer established.

Matched controls: §4.2/C.7 assert same demos, images, action space, control frequency/protocol. Table2 same scale ablation: no Pred 85.3%, no Phase78.7%, no Event66.7%, Phase-only60.0 versus90.7. Parameter count adds .841M training/.575M inference to83.87M. Exact independent capacity-matched replacement control not found.

Timing caveat: §3.3 correction happens at each query; A.6 explicitly full forward every control step with temporal ensembling. D.2 interprets H20→H10 as query-frequency change despite this; do not adopt that attribution without implementation check. DP+PACE Appendix D.6 uses eight action steps per chunk; it is not identical ACT execution.

Statistics: Wilson95% CI over 30 task rollouts (D.4); no train seed count found. Mechanistic Phase norm/contact intensity and Event/change-rate correlations are associative, not independent causal contact-state labels (§4.5). Demonstration study fixes operator/device and toggles haptics (162 episodes/condition); only 2-pin train comparison because low success without haptics on other tasks.

Limits: one arm, fixed task types, weak silicone grasps can slip and accumulate tilt; force zeroing relative first static frame is force change, not general gravity compensation. No probability-calibrated risk, held-out participant topology or independent physical-load decomposition. Artifact project existence not runtime-validated.

inclusions.synthesis: A fixed-grid optical-flow representation supplies a useful compact, spatially organized baseline. Trial-disjoint simulation evaluation isolates gravity-domain shift: Earth-trained XGBoost falls from 94.4% on Earth to 75.9% in orbit. Training across all four gravities reaches 96.3%, but that is coverage of seen domains, not novel-gravity generalization. Forty features retain 95.7%. Labels describe load-induced rotation direction in a fixed grasp; events without clear rotation or dominated by linear slip are removed. Thus this is conditional contact-event classification, not slip safety or closed-loop manipulation. The reported 0.14 ms classifier latency omits optical-flow and aggregation costs. Rigid-gel simulation, one object geometry, orientation sensitivity and no real-sensor validation bound transfer claims.

inclusions.synthesis: MorphoPlanner anchors force/proximity observations and body motion to consistently indexed material points, combines a fixed body-connectivity graph with attention, and learns next-step morphology from a tactile interaction planner. This directly broadens the archive beyond fingertip representations. Its 749K samples are simulator-generated, with a 98/1/1 split whose unit is unspecified and one listed seed. Deployment uses current sensing and a separate MorphoGuard controller. The 95.5–100% headline concerns simulated reaching among movable obstacles, 200 trials per density condition, not real bimanual manipulation success. The paper states 216 total hardware trials but provides qualitative hardware comparisons rather than a located numerical readout. Baselines differ in tactile feedback and representation; graph/attention value is not isolated. Changing obstacle counts supplies complexity extrapolation, without a predefined held-out contact-edge split or independent inter-arm load-transfer evidence.
inclusions.artifact_note: Official version1 PDF downloaded from citation_pdf_url metadata, validated %PDF header, pdfinfo and pdftotext; Fig9 visually checked. Data available on request, no runnable artifact verified.
details: Official metadata and PDF cover verify five authors, submission on October 10, posting on October 12, version 1, and DOI 10.20944/preprints202610.1082.v1. The file has a cover plus 30 printed article pages. Physical PDF page number equals printed page number plus one.

Section 2.1, printed pages 4–6: I-MP generates interaction trajectories in PyBullet. Training uses 1, 3 or 6 obstacles, fixed fractions 0, 0.5 or 1, and target coverage 0.15, 0.35 or 0.65. Failed trajectories and those exceeding 30 N are discarded. The 749K valid samples are split 98/1/1, without an explicit episode- or scene-level grouping rule.

Section 2.2, pages 6–10: current material-point positions and velocities use Fourier features and MLP encoding. Force, proximity and goals enter a fixed body-point representation. Body-connectivity/neighborhood graph convolutions, bidirectional cross-attention and self-attention predict next-step residual morphology. MorphoGuard converts this reference into joint commands. Inference uses current sensing rather than future measured state.

Section 2.3 and Table 1, page 11: AdamW, learning rate 1e-7, 100 epochs, batch size 64, and seed 42. No matched graph, tactile-modality or attention ablation was located. Unresolved references to other chapters and a draft template sentence remain, so omitted implementation details should not be inferred.

Section 3.1, pages 11–13: 356 tactile units are reported, 128 on each arm and 100 on the upper body, with matching simulator indexing. Simulated proximity comes from rays over 0–5 cm and force from engine contacts over 0–30 N. Physical sensor transduction, calibration and noise details are insufficient for a complete reproducibility audit.

Section 3.3, pages 15–18: tests vary obstacle counts from 6 to 15 and fixed fractions 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 and 0.8. The reported gap to a claimed theoretical feasibility bound is 5.59% versus 8.63% for the model-based planner. An operational procedure for establishing that bound was not located. This is complexity variation, not an explicitly held-out contact-edge topology split.

Section 3.4 and Figure 9, pages 18–19: all obstacles are movable, with 200 simulated trials per object-count condition. Success requires reaching within the time limit, force below 30 N and object stability. The 95.5–100% range is visually consistent with Figure 9. Coupled objects can cause stalling or toppling. This is low-speed reaching, not demonstrated handover or tool–workpiece cooperation.

Section 3.5, pages 20–26: sampling, B-spline and artificial-potential-field baselines use operational-cost maps. Twenty-seven conditions, 400 simulated and two real trials per condition and method yield 43,200 simulated and 216 real trials across four methods. Scenes are matched, but baselines lack the learned system’s real-time tactile/body feedback. Figure 12 reports simulation; no confidence intervals or multi-seed results were located.

Section 3.6, pages 26–27, explicitly presents qualitative hardware results in Figure 13. Section 4 limits conclusions to quasi-static or low-speed interactions. Page 28 makes data available on request. No matched-budget graph advantage or independent bilateral load attribution is established.

inclusions.title: Contact Trajectory Prompting: In-Context Transfer of Contact-Rich Behaviors from a Single Demonstration
inclusions.artifact_status: Project inspected; no runnable repository link located.
inclusions.synthesis: CTP encodes a target-object demonstration’s motion, fingertip wrenches and tactile deformation into ordered contact tokens, which current sensor observations query during single-arm execution. Its object-disjoint, one-shot tests report 78.7% success versus 65.7% for a force-augmented prompting baseline. More diagnostic ablations separate reference contact as behavior specification from online contact as feedback: position-only references lose graded wiping-intensity ordering, while removing current contact sharply harms height-perturbed execution. The method strengthens the case for temporally structured contact references without establishing bimanual role structure or topology transfer. Deployment requires a target-object demonstration; dense tactile inputs are deformation proxies. Baselines share task data and evaluation but not all architectural or adaptation budgets, and training-seed uncertainty is unreported.

inclusions.title: ForceWAM: Decoupling Future and Response Learning from Demo and Play Data for Contact-Rich Manipulation
inclusions.artifact_status: Official project inspected; code listed as forthcoming, no runnable artifact verified.
inclusions.synthesis: ForceWAM separates a task-trained visual–wrench future generator from an inverse-dynamics executor trained on demonstrations and exploratory play. Recorded futures supervise the executor offline; generated futures and causal measured wrench feedback drive real single-arm deployment. Holding task demonstrations, ForceWM and optimizer updates fixed, adding play raises success by 15–45 percentage points across sliding, flipping and ring placement, although total experience increases. A shared-data ablation supports joint visual and wrench futures over either alone. These results favor temporally explicit contact-outcome conditioning and broader execution learning. They do not establish tactile spatial structure, bimanual transfer or topology OOD; wrench prediction evidence is qualitative and training-seed/success uncertainty is unreported. The project lists code as forthcoming.

inclusions.artifact_status: Official project redirect followed; code listed as forthcoming, no runnable artifact verified.
inclusions.synthesis: ILA makes joint motion–tactile latents the action target on a real dual-arm platform, including plate holding and wiping. Its encoder learns from complete recorded chunks; deployment predicts latents from chunk-start observations and executes 128 actions before replanning. Representation ablations retain policy touch while removing tactile latent supervision, supporting contact-aware targets beyond tactile inputs. Held-out-trajectory probes and separate causal-input future-prediction tests add evidence beyond success, but probe intervals exclude training-seed variation. Headline comparisons also add visual dynamics tokens; force quantities are sensor-native deformation proxies. Offline rewards use realized tactile outcomes and expert references without becoming online observations or calibrated success probabilities. Mixed cut-versus-rollout success units, manual force-profile alignment and absent topology holdout limit generalization claims.

DeTac predicts shading and marker images jointly from one mixed tactile image, with marker-neighborhood and cross-branch consistency supervision. Its real aligned pairs improve the grounding of the image-separation problem. inclusions.synthesis: Include as a tactile-observable geometric estimator and a useful negative-control example. TacSpin retains local contact depth/shear fields, estimates rotation axis and magnitude separately, refines using boundary circulation, and fuses two opposing fingertip responses. AprilTag poses supervise calibration and evaluation only. Matched calibration splits and a full-matrix TacSE3 control make the fixed-axis gain more interpretable.
